1	/**
2	 * File-finding evaluation runner.
3	 *
4	 * For each task mined from a repository's bug-fix history: prepare a worktree
5	 * with the fix's source reverted, confirm the fix's tests fail, run the agent
6	 * headless through the shipped base profile with the failing output as its
7	 * task, re-run the tests, and record file-finding metrics from the session.
8	 *
9	 * Usage:
10	 *   pnpm run eval:file-finding -- --repo <git repo> [--limit 10] [--out eval-results]
11	 *     [--install "pnpm install --prefer-offline"] [--keep] [--dry-run]
12	 *
13	 * `--dry-run` stops after preparing and validating each task, so it needs no
14	 * model key. A full run needs the provider key (DEEPSEEK_API_KEY by default).
15	 */
16	
17	import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
18	import { copyFile, mkdir, rm, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises'
19	import { tmpdir } from 'node:os'
20	import { join, resolve } from 'node:path'
21	import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url'
22	import { parseArgs } from 'node:util'
23	import { resolveExampleLaunch } from '@deepseek-ai/dsh-loader-smoke'
24	import { computeMetrics, summarize } from './metrics.ts'
25	import type { EvalEvent, EvalUsage, RunMetrics } from './metrics.ts'
26	import { mineTasks, prepareWorkspace, removeWorkspace, taskPrompt } from './tasks.ts'
27	import type { EvalTask } from './tasks.ts'
28	
29	const repoRoot = fileURLToPath(new URL('../../', import.meta.url))
30	const DRIVER = join(repoRoot, 'packages/test-support/loader-smoke/tests/fixtures/base-driver.ts')
31	const OVERLAY = join(repoRoot, 'scripts/eval/eval.cordis.yml')
32	const TSCONFIG = join(repoRoot, 'tsconfig.json')
33	const MAX_FAILURE_CHARS = 6_000
34	const LOCALE_FILE = /(^|\/)locales?(\/|\.ts$|\.tsx$)/
35	
36	/** Outcome of one task. */
37	interface TaskResult {
38	  readonly task: EvalTask
39	  readonly status: 'valid' | 'invalid' | 'ran' | 'error'
40	  readonly passed: boolean
41	  readonly metrics?: RunMetrics
42	  readonly finalText?: string
43	  readonly note?: string
44	}
45	
46	interface Command {
47	  readonly code: number | null
48	  readonly stdout: string
49	  readonly stderr: string
50	}
51	
52	function exec(command: string, args: readonly string[], cwd: string, env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, timeoutMs: number): Promise<Command> {
53	  return new Promise((resolvePromise) => {
54	    const child = spawn(command, args, { cwd, env, shell: process.platform === 'win32' && !command.endsWith('.exe'), stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'] })
55	    let stdout = ''
56	    let stderr = ''
57	    child.stdout.setEncoding('utf8').on('data', (chunk: string) => { stdout += chunk })
58	    child.stderr.setEncoding('utf8').on('data', (chunk: string) => { stderr += chunk })
59	    const timer = setTimeout(() => { child.kill('SIGKILL') }, timeoutMs)
60	    child.on('close', (code) => {
61	      clearTimeout(timer)
62	      resolvePromise({ code, stdout, stderr })
63	    })
64	  })
65	}
66	
67	function runTests(workspace: string, files: readonly string[]): Promise<Command> {
68	  return exec('npx', ['vitest', 'run', ...files], workspace, process.env, 15 * 60_000)
69	}
70	
71	function tail(text: string, max: number): string {
72	  return text.length <= max ? text : `[... ${text.length - max} earlier characters omitted ...]\n${text.slice(-max)}`
73	}
74	
75	/** Parse the driver's JSONL stdout into session events and the final result row. */
76	function parseDriverOutput(stdout: string): { events: EvalEvent[]; usage?: EvalUsage; output?: string } {
77	  const events: EvalEvent[] = []
78	  let usage: EvalUsage | undefined
79	  let output: string | undefined
80	  for (const line of stdout.split('\n')) {
81	    if (!line.startsWith('{')) continue
82	    let row: { type?: string; event?: EvalEvent; usage?: EvalUsage; output?: string }
83	    try {
84	      row = JSON.parse(line) as typeof row
85	    } catch {
86	      // Non-JSON log lines from plugins are not events.
87	      continue
88	    }
89	    if (row.type === 'session_event' && row.event !== undefined) events.push(row.event)
90	    if (row.type === 'result') {
91	      usage = row.usage
92	      output = row.output
93	    }
94	  }
95	  return { events, ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage }, ...output === undefined ? {} : { output } }
96	}
97	
98	/** The error message of a turn that ended in error, e.g. a model provider rejecting every request. */
99	function turnErrorOf(events: readonly EvalEvent[]): string | undefined {
100	  for (const event of events) {
101	    if (event.type !== 'turn/end') continue
102	    const reason = event.data.reason as { kind?: string; error?: { message?: string } } | undefined
103	    if (reason?.kind === 'error') return reason.error?.message ?? 'unknown error'
104	  }
105	  return undefined
106	}
107	
108	interface RunOptions {
109	  readonly repo: string
110	  readonly install: string
111	  readonly keep: boolean
112	  readonly dryRun: boolean
113	  /** Existing DSH home whose settings and stored credentials the agent run should use. */
114	  readonly homeFrom?: string
115	}
116	
117	/** Files copied from `--home-from`: provider settings and the credential store they reference. */
118	const HOME_FILES = ['settings.yaml', '.credentials.yaml']
119	
120	async function runTask(task: EvalTask, options: RunOptions): Promise<TaskResult> {
121	  const workspace = join(tmpdir(), `dsh-eval-${task.id}`)
122	  // Kept outside the repository and deleted after the task, since it may hold copied credentials.
123	  const home = join(tmpdir(), `dsh-eval-home-${task.id}`)
124	  await rm(workspace, { recursive: true, force: true })
125	  await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true })
126	  try {
127	    await prepareWorkspace(options.repo, task, workspace)
128	    const [installCommand = 'pnpm', ...installArgs] = options.install.split(' ')
129	    const install = await exec(installCommand, installArgs, workspace, process.env, 30 * 60_000)
130	    if (install.code !== 0) return { task, status: 'error', passed: false, note: `install failed: ${tail(install.stderr, 800)}` }
131	
132	    const baseline = await runTests(workspace, task.testFiles)
133	    if (baseline.code === 0) {
134	      return { task, status: 'invalid', passed: false, note: `tests pass without the fix:\n${tail(baseline.stdout, 1_500)}` }
135	    }
136	    if (options.dryRun) return { task, status: 'valid', passed: false, note: 'dry run: prepared and validated' }
137	
138	    await mkdir(home, { recursive: true })
139	    if (options.homeFrom !== undefined) {
140	      for (const file of HOME_FILES) {
141	        await copyFile(join(options.homeFrom, file), join(home, file)).catch((error: unknown) => {
142	          if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'ENOENT') throw error
143	        })
144	      }
145	    }
146	    const launch = resolveExampleLaunch({
147	      srcBin: DRIVER,
148	      libBin: DRIVER,
149	      mode: 'src',
150	      tsconfigPath: TSCONFIG,
151	      configArgs: [JSON.stringify([OVERLAY]), taskPrompt(task, tail(`${baseline.stdout}\n${baseline.stderr}`, MAX_FAILURE_CHARS))],
152	      env: { DSH_HOME: home, DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED: '1' },
153	    })
154	    const agent = await exec(launch.command, launch.args, workspace, { ...process.env, ...launch.env }, 60 * 60_000)
155	    const parsed = parseDriverOutput(agent.stdout)
156	    const turnError = turnErrorOf(parsed.events)
157	    if (turnError !== undefined) return { task, status: 'error', passed: false, note: `agent turn failed: ${turnError}` }
158	    const after = await runTests(workspace, task.testFiles)
159	    const metrics = computeMetrics(parsed.events, { workspace, sourceFiles: task.sourceFiles, testFiles: task.testFiles }, parsed.usage)
160	    return {
161	      task,
162	      status: 'ran',
163	      passed: after.code === 0 && !metrics.editedTests,
164	      metrics,
165	      ...parsed.output === undefined ? {} : { finalText: parsed.output },
166	      ...agent.code === 0 ? {} : { note: `driver exited ${String(agent.code)}: ${tail(agent.stderr, 800)}` },
167	    }
168	  } catch (error: unknown) {
169	    return { task, status: 'error', passed: false, note: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error) }
170	  } finally {
171	    await rm(home, { recursive: true, force: true })
172	    if (!options.keep) await removeWorkspace(options.repo, workspace).catch(() => rm(workspace, { recursive: true, force: true }))
173	  }
174	}
175	
176	function markdownTable(results: readonly TaskResult[]): string {
177	  const rows = results.map(result => [
178	    result.task.id,
179	    result.status,
180	    result.passed ? 'yes' : 'no',
181	    result.metrics?.editedExpected === true ? 'yes' : 'no',
182	    String(result.metrics?.firstSeenStep ?? '-'),
183	    String(result.metrics?.firstReadStep ?? '-'),
184	    String(result.metrics?.steps ?? '-'),
185	    String(result.metrics?.usage?.inputTokens ?? '-'),
186	    result.task.subject.replaceAll('|', '/').slice(0, 60),
187	  ].join(' | '))
188	  return [
189	    '| task | status | passed | right file edited | first seen step | first read step | steps | input tokens | subject |',
190	    '|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|',
191	    ...rows.map(row => `| ${row} |`),
192	  ].join('\n')
193	}
194	
195	async function main(): Promise<void> {
196	  const argv = process.argv.slice(2)
197	  const { values } = parseArgs({
198	    // `pnpm run eval:file-finding -- --repo …` forwards the separator itself.
199	    args: argv[0] === '--' ? argv.slice(1) : argv,
200	    options: {
201	      repo: { type: 'string' },
202	      limit: { type: 'string', default: '10' },
203	      out: { type: 'string', default: 'eval-results' },
204	      install: { type: 'string', default: 'pnpm install --prefer-offline' },
205	      keep: { type: 'boolean', default: false },
206	      'dry-run': { type: 'boolean', default: false },
207	      'home-from': { type: 'string' },
208	      only: { type: 'string' },
209	    },
210	  })
211	  if (values.repo === undefined) throw new Error('--repo <git repository with bug-fix history> is required')
212	  const dryRun = values['dry-run']
213	  const homeFrom = values['home-from'] === undefined ? undefined : resolve(values['home-from'])
214	  if (!dryRun && homeFrom === undefined && process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY === undefined) {
215	    throw new Error('no model credentials: set DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, pass --home-from <dsh home>, or use --dry-run')
216	  }
217	  const repo = resolve(values.repo)
218	  const out = resolve(values.out)
219	  await mkdir(out, { recursive: true })
220	
221	  const limit = Number(values.limit)
222	  const only = values.only?.split(',').map(id => id.trim()).filter(Boolean)
223	  const tasks = (await mineTasks(repo, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER))
224	    .filter(task => !task.sourceFiles.every(file => LOCALE_FILE.test(file)))
225	    .filter(task => only === undefined || only.some(id => task.fixCommit.startsWith(id)))
226	    .slice(0, limit)
227	  process.stdout.write(`eval: ${tasks.length} task(s) from ${repo}${dryRun ? ' (dry run)' : ''}\n`)
228	
229	  const results: TaskResult[] = []
230	  for (const task of tasks) {
231	    process.stdout.write(`eval: ${task.id} ${task.subject}\n`)
232	    const result = await runTask(task, {
233	      repo,
234	      install: values.install,
235	      keep: values.keep,
236	      dryRun,
237	      ...homeFrom === undefined ? {} : { homeFrom },
238	    })
239	    results.push(result)
240	    await writeFile(join(out, `${task.id}.json`), `${JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)}\n`)
241	    process.stdout.write(`eval: ${task.id} -> ${result.status}${result.passed ? ' (passed)' : ''}${result.note === undefined ? '' : ` — ${result.note.split('\n')[0]}`}\n`)
242	  }
243	
244	  const ran = results.flatMap(result => result.status === 'ran' && result.metrics !== undefined
245	    ? [{ passed: result.passed, metrics: result.metrics }]
246	    : [])
247	  const summary = { tasks: results.length, byStatus: countBy(results.map(result => result.status)), ...summarize(ran) }
248	  await writeFile(join(out, 'summary.json'), `${JSON.stringify(summary, null, 2)}\n`)
249	  await writeFile(join(out, 'summary.md'), `${markdownTable(results)}\n`)
250	  process.stdout.write(`${JSON.stringify(summary, null, 2)}\n`)
251	}
252	
253	function countBy(values: readonly string[]): Record<string, number> {
254	  const counts: Record<string, number> = {}
255	  for (const value of values) counts[value] = (counts[value] ?? 0) + 1
256	  return counts
257	}
258	
259	await main()

1	# Agent Note: A file-finding evaluation gates code-navigation features
2	
3	Status: implemented
4	
5	## Problem
6	
7	Several navigation features were proposed — symbol tools, a code graph with blast-radius queries, git co-change ranking, stack-trace seeding — each promising that the agent finds the right file faster. None could be justified or compared without evidence of how the agent performs today, and the decision was to build them only if they measurably help. The repository had no way to measure file-finding: snapshot tests replay recorded sessions and real-API tests check narrow behaviors.
8	
9	## Decision
10	
11	`scripts/eval/` mines tasks from a repository's bug-fix history, runs the agent on each, and records file-finding metrics.
12	
13	- **Tasks.** A qualifying fix commit changes 1–3 source files and at least one spec file within 12 changed files; locale-only fixes are skipped. The task workspace is a detached worktree at the fix commit with its source files restored to the parent, so the fix's own tests fail. A task whose tests already pass is dropped.
14	- **Prompt.** The agent receives only the failing test output and an instruction not to edit tests — not the commit subject or source paths — like a CI failure report.
15	- **Run.** The headless base driver used by recorded snapshots boots the shipped base profile with `scripts/eval/eval.cordis.yml`: model from `DSH_EVAL_PROVIDER`/`DSH_EVAL_MODEL`, workspace-write sandboxing, approvals `never`, uncompressed logs.
16	- **Metrics.** Computed from the streamed session events: pass, right-file edited, first step that saw or read a fix file, reads before the correct read, steps, tool calls, extra edits, test edits, and token usage.
17	
18	`pnpm run eval:file-finding -- --repo <path> [--dry-run]` runs it. This repository's history is squashed to 17 commits, so tasks come from a repository with real history; a blobless clone of upstream `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` yields 1,751 candidates before the locale filter.
19	
20	## Alternatives considered
21	
22	**Hand-written tasks.** Fully controllable, but slow to write and biased toward what the author thinks is hard. Mined fixes come with a real answer (the diff) and real tests.
23	
24	**SWE-bench.** A standard benchmark, but in Python repositories unlike the TypeScript codebases this harness is used on, and it needs Docker images per task. It can be added later as a second task source.
25	
26	**Measuring in the web app.** Fidelity would be highest, but runs would need a browser and could not be scripted in bulk; the base driver is already the recorded-snapshot path.
27	
28	## Consequences
29	
30	- Navigation features get a before/after number on the same tasks instead of an argument.
31	- A full run needs a model key and installs dependencies per task, so it is slow and costs tokens; `--dry-run` validates tasks without a key.
32	- The failing test paths hint at the package, so the numbers measure finding the file within a package more than across the repository.
33	- The base profile differs from the web presets in compaction mounting, so results describe the agent loop and tools more than web-specific behavior.
34

1	# File-finding evaluation
2	
3	Measures how well the agent finds and fixes the right code before any navigation feature (symbol tools, a code graph, co-change ranking) is built. A feature ships only if it moves these numbers.
4	
5	## How a task is made
6	
7	Tasks come from a repository's own bug-fix history. A commit qualifies when its subject reads like a fix (or it adds a `bug-fix` Agent Note), it changes 1–3 package or app source files, it changes at least one `tests/**/*.spec.ts` file, and it touches at most 12 files. Tasks that only change locale files are skipped, because a copy edit says little about file-finding.
8	
9	For each task the runner:
10	
11	1. checks out the fix commit in a detached git worktree and restores the source files to the parent commit, keeping the fix's tests;
12	2. installs dependencies and runs those tests, and drops the task if they already pass;
13	3. gives the agent the failing test output as its only instruction — the source files and the commit subject are not revealed;
14	4. runs the agent headless through the shipped base profile (`packages/test-support/loader-smoke/tests/fixtures/base-driver.ts` with [`eval.cordis.yml`](eval.cordis.yml));
15	5. re-runs the tests and computes metrics from the streamed session events.
16	
17	## Metrics
18	
19	| Metric | Meaning |
20	|---|---|
21	| passed | The fix's tests pass afterwards and no test file was edited |
22	| right file edited | At least one of the real fix's source files was edited |
23	| first seen step | First step whose search results or reads named a real fix file |
24	| first read step | First step that read a real fix file |
25	| reads before correct | `read` calls before that first correct read |
26	| steps, tool calls, input tokens | Cost of the run |
27	| extra edits | Files edited that are neither fix sources nor tests |
28	
29	`summary.json` aggregates pass count, correct-file count, and medians; `summary.md` is a per-task table; `<task>.json` holds each run's full metrics and final answer.
30	
31	## Running it
32	
33	```sh
34	# Prepare and validate tasks only; no model key needed.
35	pnpm run eval:file-finding -- --repo <path-to-repo> --limit 5 --dry-run
36	
37	# Full run; needs DEEPSEEK_API_KEY (model via DSH_EVAL_PROVIDER / DSH_EVAL_MODEL).
38	pnpm run eval:file-finding -- --repo <path-to-repo> --limit 20 --out eval-results
39	```
40	
41	This repository's history is squashed, so mine a repository with real history, such as a clone of the upstream `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`. A blobless clone (`git clone --filter=blob:none`) is enough. `--install` overrides the dependency command, and `--keep` leaves worktrees in place for inspection.
42	
43	## Limits
44	
45	- The agent runs the base profile with workspace-write sandboxing and no approval prompts; the web presets add their own compaction rows, so compaction behavior can differ slightly from the web app.
46	- The prompt names the failing test files, which hints at the package; the metrics measure finding the source file within that hint.
47	- One run per task is noisy. Compare feature variants on the same tasks and several runs before drawing conclusions.
48

2	 * File-finding metrics computed from one agent run's session events.
3	 *
4	 * Pure: the runner streams canonical session events from the base driver and

10	/** The subset of a canonical session event the metrics read. */
11	export interface EvalEvent {
12	  readonly type: string
13	  readonly data: Record<string, unknown>
14	}

16	/** Token totals reported by the driver's result line. */

54	const READ_TOOLS = new Set(['read'])
55	const EDIT_TOOLS = new Set(['edit', 'write', 'str_replace_editor'])

57	/**
58	 * Compute the metrics for one run.
59	 * @param events - the run's session events in log order.
60	 * @param expected - the task's workspace and real-fix files.
61	 * @param usage - token totals from the driver's result line, when reported.
62	 * @returns the run's metrics.
63	 */
64	export function computeMetrics(
65	  events: readonly EvalEvent[],
66	  expected: EvalExpectation,
67	  usage?: EvalUsage,
68	): RunMetrics {
69	  const sources = new Set(expected.sourceFiles)
70	  const tests = new Set(expected.testFiles)
71	  const toolCalls: Record<string, number> = {}
72	  const edited = new Set<string>()
73	  const found = { step: 0, steps: 0, seen: null as number | null, read: null as number | null, readsBefore: 0 }
74	
75	  const noteSeen = (): void => { found.seen ??= found.step }
76	  const visitCall = (name: string, args: unknown): void => {
77	    toolCalls[name] = (toolCalls[name] ?? 0) + 1
78	    const path = workspacePath(expected.workspace, filePathOf(args))
79	    if (READ_TOOLS.has(name)) {
80	      if (path !== undefined && sources.has(path)) {
81	        found.read ??= found.step
82	        noteSeen()
83	      } else if (found.read === null) {
84	        found.readsBefore += 1
85	      }
86	    }
87	    if (EDIT_TOOLS.has(name) && path !== undefined) edited.add(path)
88	  }
89	
90	  for (const event of events) {
91	    switch (event.type) {
92	      case 'step/start':
93	        found.step = typeof event.data.step === 'number' ? event.data.step : found.step + 1
94	        found.steps += 1
95	        break
96	      case 'tool/call':
97	        visitCall(String(event.data.name), parseArguments(event.data.arguments))
98	        break
99	      case 'tool/code-dispatch':
100	        visitCall(String(event.data.name), event.data.arguments)
101	        if (found.seen === null && mentionsAny(event.data.content, expected.sourceFiles)) noteSeen()
102	        break
103	      case 'tool/result':
104	        if (found.seen === null && mentionsAny(resultContent(event.data), expected.sourceFiles)) noteSeen()
105	        break
106	      default:
107	        break
108	    }
109	  }
110	
111	  const editedFiles = [...edited].sort()
112	  return {
113	    steps: found.steps,
114	    toolCalls,
115	    firstSeenStep: found.seen,
116	    firstReadStep: found.read,
117	    readsBeforeCorrect: found.readsBefore,
118	    editedFiles,
119	    editedExpected: editedFiles.some(file => sources.has(file)),
120	    extraEdits: editedFiles.filter(file => !sources.has(file) && !tests.has(file)),
121	    editedTests: editedFiles.some(file => tests.has(file)),
122	    ...usage === undefined ? {} : { usage },
123	  }
124	}

126	/**
127	 * Resolve a tool-supplied path to a workspace-relative `/`-separated path.
128	 * @param workspace - the run's workspace root.
129	 * @param path - the path the model passed, absolute or relative.
130	 * @returns the relative path, or undefined when absent or outside the workspace.
131	 */
132	export function workspacePath(workspace: string, path: string | undefined): string | undefined {
133	  if (path === undefined) return undefined
134	  const rel = relative(workspace, resolve(workspace, path))
135	  if (rel === '' || rel.startsWith('..') || isAbsolute(rel)) return undefined
136	  return rel.split('\\').join('/')
137	}
138	
139	function parseArguments(raw: unknown): unknown {
140	  if (typeof raw !== 'string') return raw
141	  try {
142	    return JSON.parse(raw) as unknown
143	  } catch {
144	    // Malformed model-written arguments name no file.
145	    return undefined
146	  }
147	}
148	
149	function filePathOf(args: unknown): string | undefined {
150	  if (typeof args !== 'object' || args === null) return undefined
151	  const record = args as Record<string, unknown>
152	  const path = record.file_path ?? record.path
153	  return typeof path === 'string' && path.length > 0 ? path : undefined
154	}
155	
156	function resultContent(data: Record<string, unknown>): unknown {
157	  const message = data.message as { content?: Array<{ content?: unknown }> } | undefined
158	  return message?.content?.[0]?.content
159	}
160	
161	function mentionsAny(content: unknown, files: readonly string[]): boolean {
162	  const text = JSON.stringify(content ?? '').split('\\\\').join('/')
163	  return files.some(file => text.includes(file))
164	}

181	export function summarize(results: readonly { readonly passed: boolean; readonly metrics: RunMetrics }[]): MetricsSummary {
182	  return {

184	    passed: results.filter(result => result.passed).length,
185	    editedExpected: results.filter(result => result.metrics.editedExpected).length,
186	    medianFirstReadStep: median(results.flatMap(result => result.metrics.firstReadStep ?? [])),
187	    medianSteps: median(results.map(result => result.metrics.steps)),
188	    totalInputTokens: results.reduce((total, result) => total + (result.metrics.usage?.inputTokens ?? 0), 0),
189	  }

192	function median(values: readonly number[]): number | null {
193	  if (values.length === 0) return null
194	  const sorted = [...values].sort((a, b) => a - b)
195	  const mid = Math.floor(sorted.length / 2)
196	  const upper = sorted[mid] ?? 0
197	  return sorted.length % 2 === 1 ? upper : ((sorted[mid - 1] ?? 0) + upper) / 2
198	}
